clue.text: With sub-zero temperatures around, start of winter unpleasantly close

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the other piece sits inside the outer word
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only one letter of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: weather below freezing is frosty
opening letter of winter

explanation.surface: A winter's day that is freezing yet somehow muggy and stuffy indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Frowsty describes a room that is stuffy and stale-smelling, airless in an unpleasant way.

clue.text: Old woman creating mouldy smell that holds operations up

indicators.note: one word holds the other by gripping it inside
in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: fust is a musty, mouldy smell
ops is short for operations; going up it reads SPO

explanation.surface: An elderly woman's musty house smells so bad it stalls surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' is not literal: it is a jibe for a fussy person of either sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone an old woman means they fret over trifles, which is exactly a fusspot.

clue.text: Carriage that's damaged in hartal left abandoned

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
the abbreviation for left is abandoned, dropped from the word

blocks.note: a hartal is an Indian strike; it loses its L before the rearranging
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A carriage is wrecked during a general strike, and its owners flee.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratha is an Indian four-wheeled carriage, often ox-drawn, also a temple chariot.

clue.text: Smell worse than what pigs produce, volume formerly inside

indicators.note: the last pieces named go inside the earlier word

blocks.note: the noise a pig makes
V is the symbol for volume
erst is an old word for formerly

explanation.surface: A farmer complains that something reeks worse than his pigsty, as it used to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what pigs produce' points at manure, but it is the sound they make.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstink is to stink more than something else, an old Shakespearean coinage.

clue.text: One demonstrating bathroom appliance?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who shows something
second meaning: the spray fitting you wash under

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently; the question mark flags the punning one.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who shows things is literally a shower, and the bathroom fitting has the same spelling.

clue.text: Sluggish business receiving a right taunt

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the later pieces go inside the first

blocks.note: trade as commerce
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
a dig is a sneering remark

explanation.surface: A slow-moving firm gets mocked for its sluggishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardigrade means slow-paced, from the Latin for slow-stepping, and names the tiny water bears.

clue.text: One bit of wreckage, wood floating helplessly

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a single letter of it, here the first

blocks.note: one as the article a
first letter of wreckage
ash is a timber tree

explanation.surface: A lone piece of a shipwreck, a timber, drifts at the mercy of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awash is covered by or tossed about in water, at the mercy of the waves.

clue.text: Immigrants when receiving legal right

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the second piece goes inside the first

blocks.note: as in the sense of while or when
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Newcomers to a country are granted their entitlements under the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens are people from another country living as foreigners, which immigrants are.

clue.text: Pad soaking in old dyestuff

indicators.note: a pad soaking in a liquid takes it inside itself

blocks.note: a wad is a pad of soft material
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A cotton pad lies steeping in an ancient dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Woad is a blue dye made from a plant, famously used by ancient Britons.

clue.text: Steamer you'll find isn't under pressure as formerly

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece named second is placed below the first

blocks.note: str. is the dictionary abbreviation for steamer
ain't is a nonstandard form of isn't

explanation.surface: A steamship is reassuringly said not to be at risk of a boiler blowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steamer' wants to be a vessel whole, but Azed uses its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Straint is an obsolete Spenserian word for pressure or strain.

clue.text: Old vow — see me freed from the same when it's broken

indicators.note: freed from means let out of, so those letters leave the phrase
broken means smashed into pieces that are put back in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reminder of an old promise: keep your word to me, as before.
explanation.definitionFit: Heast is an obsolete form of hest, a behest or vow.

clue.text: One sort of tart or another, and the rest doing a turn outside

definitions.text: One sort of tart or another

indicators.note: to do a turn is to face the other way, so the phrase's letters run backwards
the turned letters sit on either side of the other piece, wrapping it

blocks.note: et cetera means and the rest; the turn makes it CTE, split around the other piece
tart as slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A baker lists the tarts on offer, then dismisses everything else on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition does double duty: a harlot is one kind of tart, a charlotte is a pudding, another kind; so 'One sort of tart or another' covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a fruit dessert baked in a mould lined with bread or sponge, loosely another sort of tart.

clue.text: Stop the race

blocks.note: first meaning: to check or staunch a flow
second meaning: a line of descent, a family stock

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an order to halt a sporting event, but race here means lineage, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem bleeding is to stop it, and a stem is also the main line of a family's ancestry.

clue.text: Something to revive libido by way of innate character dropping in

indicators.note: dropping here means letting fall away, and the two letters spelling in are the ones let go

blocks.note: via means by way of
going against the grain means against one's nature

explanation.surface: Advice that a lagging sex drive comes back once your true nature reasserts itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping in' looks like visiting, but it means GRAIN loses its IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Viagra is the trade name of a drug prescribed for erectile dysfunction, popularly a sex-life booster.

clue.text: Ivy rampant round cedar I'll cut — record kept by camcorder? (10, two words)

indicators.note: rampant ivy grows wild and unruly, so its letters run riot
round puts the first piece on either side of what follows
to cut into something is to enter its middle

blocks.note: taken as written, scrambled and split around the rest
the deodar is a Himalayan cedar
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener vows to hack back ivy smothering a cedar, filming the work as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cedar' is not wordplay fodder; it is defined by a specific cedar species.
explanation.definitionFit: A video diary is a personal record filmed regularly on a camcorder; the question mark admits it is one example.

clue.text: Crafty fellow making troublesome woman stamp

blocks.note: a shrew is a scolding, bad-tempered woman
a die is a tool that stamps a design

explanation.surface: A sly man turns an awkward woman into a postage stamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrewdie is an informal word for a shrewd, cunning person.

clue.text: Dart fired to wound etc he felt being smitten

indicators.note: smitten means struck hard, and struck letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man struck by Cupid's dart describes the pain of falling in love.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the definition is love-struck feeling; it is a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A flechette is a small steel dart dropped or fired as a weapon, notably from aircraft in the First World War.

clue.text: Something for the sandwiches went steadily? Sounds like it

indicators.note: the solver is told the answer, spoken, matches the phrase before it

blocks.note: to pace is to walk at a steady rate

explanation.surface: A puzzled cook wonders whether walking at an even tempo is a sandwich ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish or meat paste is a spread commonly put in sandwiches.

clue.text: Move unsteadily, following drunk

blocks.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone staggers about after a heavy night's drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives flit the sense of being unsteady or fluttering, not only moving house.
explanation.definitionFit: To flit is to flutter or move lightly and erratically from place to place.

clue.text: 'Grand' French palace: king will be seen in it when erected, shortly

indicators.note: a thing seen in another sits inside it
erected means stood upright, so in a down clue the letters read upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
R for rex, king
anon means soon, shortly

explanation.surface: A guidebook explains that the king will soon visit his grand palace once it is built.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around Grand hint at its name: the Grand Trianon at Versailles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Trianon is a small palace in the park at Versailles, built for Louis XIV.

clue.text: Time is pressing with red swelling

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
urges means presses or impels
from 'not a red cent', a cent as the coin

explanation.surface: A doctor warns that an inflamed, reddening lump needs urgent attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' reads as the colour of the swelling, but it stands for a cent, the copper coin in 'not a red cent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Turgescent means becoming swollen or distended, as tissue does when filled with fluid.

clue.text: Without mincing words, group gathered in enters Elysium

indicators.note: a group gathered in is enclosed by the words around it, so the letters are inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A blunt account of the blessed arriving in paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking tersely means bluntly and briefly, using few words and no softening.

clue.text: Like French flag, splendid, held by trim CO, fluttering

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it
fluttering letters flap about out of place, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
rich as sumptuous or splendid

explanation.surface: A smart commanding officer salutes the grand tricolour as it waves in the breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Trichromic means having three colours, as the blue, white and red tricolour does.

clue.text: Rainy day spent in deathly rambling

indicators.note: something spent is used up and gone
rambling wanders all over, so the letters stray from their order

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for day
taken as written, losing its D

explanation.surface: A wet day passed in gloomy, aimless wandering.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyetal is a technical term meaning relating to rain or rainfall, from the Greek for rain.

clue.text: Subway systems: put 'em in order, from below

indicators.note: in a down clue reading from the bottom means the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to sort them is to put them in order, with 'em for them

explanation.surface: A transport planner arranges a city's underground lines, starting from the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a subway is a pedestrian underpass; here it means an underground railway, as in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Metros are underground urban railway networks, what Americans call subways.

clue.text: Hit the jackpot with 1,000 a second?

blocks.note: to hit the jackpot is to win
K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: A gambler imagines winnings pouring in at a thousand pounds every second.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: 'in a wink' means in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: A wink is used for a moment or an instant, as in 'I didn't sleep a wink'.

clue.text: Pimple, what the most incompetent will fail to shift?

definitions.text: what the most incompetent will fail to shift?

blocks.note: first meaning: a pustule, an old sense of the word

blocks.clueFragment: what the most incompetent will fail to shift?
blocks.note: second meaning: the shellfish sold at a seaside stall

explanation.walkthrough: A hopeless person is said to be unable to run a whelk stall; to shift goods is to sell them.
explanation.definitionFit: A whelk is both an edible sea snail and, in an older sense, a pimple or pustule.

clue.text: Former magistrate brought back hanging, hard at heart

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the word runs the other way
at heart puts the letter in the middle of the other word

blocks.note: the hangman's noose; turned round it reads EPOR
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An old judge restores the death penalty, showing a hard heart.
explanation.definitionFit: An ephor was one of five senior magistrates of ancient Sparta.

clue.text: 'E mebbe deals in knitwear, such as goes into a basket

definitions.text: such as goes into a basket

indicators.note: a Cockney says 'e for he, dropping the opening aitch, so the next word loses it too

blocks.note: a hosier sells stockings and knitted goods

explanation.surface: Speculation in dialect that a certain man sells woollens, perhaps in wicker baskets.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow whose pliant shoots are woven into baskets.

clue.text: Scottish set creating stir locally on loch

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it

blocks.note: jee is a Scots word for to stir or budge
L is the map abbreviation for loch

explanation.surface: A group of Scots makes a commotion out on a loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like a group of people, but it is the verb, as jelly sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeel is a Scots verb meaning to congeal or jell, so in Scotland a jelly is said to jeel.

clue.text: With year gone, I dye frizzy hair? Brown perhaps

indicators.note: with something gone it is taken away, here the abbreviation for year

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for year
taken as written, losing its Y and then jumbled
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone colouring their frizzy hair asks whether brown would be the right shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a hair colour, but it is Tina Brown, the British-born editor of Vanity Fair and The New Yorker.

clue.text: Ditsy teen, with another one only half besotted

blocks.note: taken as written
another teen, of which only the first half counts

clue.text: Old-fashioned pen starts to splash the ink everywhere

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, taken from each word that follows

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.definitionFit: Stie is an obsolete spelling of sty; Chambers files it under the climbing verb, so the pigpen sense is a slight stretch.

clue.text: Fine quartz crystal suggesting Cupid's dart

definitions.text: Fine quartz crystal suggesting Cupid's dart

blocks.note: surface reading: a gemstone with delicate needles inside
setter's reading: the mineral's name evokes the weapon of the god of love

explanation.walkthrough: Hair-fine needles of rutile in quartz look like tiny darts, so the stone is named after Cupid's weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The love-arrow is a needle-like rutile crystal enclosed in rock crystal, also called Venus's hair-stone.

clue.text: King with royal mistress? This marks one's passing

blocks.note: K for king, as in chess
Nell Gwyn, mistress of Charles II

explanation.surface: A king and his mistress, and something solemn at his end.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the bell tolled to announce a death or a funeral.

clue.text: Shakespeare's skill, an inexplicable phenomenon

blocks.note: first meaning: a craft or trade, as Shakespeare used the word
second meaning: something nobody can explain

explanation.walkthrough: The trade sense comes from the old word for a craft guild, as in the mystery plays.
